paragraphs: Swamiji recalled an old tale. In India drinking alcohol was considered very wrong. One night two brothers decided to drink in secret, but their uncle, a strict and orthodox man, was asleep in the very next room.
Before they started, they agreed to stay absolutely quiet so their uncle would not wake.

Once the drinking began, each kept reminding the other to be silent or uncle would wake up. Each tried to hush the other more loudly, until they were shouting. Of course the uncle woke, walked in and caught them red-handed.

Swamiji said many of us behave just like those drunken brothers when we shout about universal brotherhood. We declare that everyone is equal, and then we form a sect, and the moment we do that, equality is gone. He pointed out that religions loudly preach brotherhood, yet those outside the fold are often left out, threatened or condemned. The louder the slogan, the less of it seems to survive in practice.
learn: It's easy to post about unity and equality; living it is harder. Notice when your groups, labels or circles quietly shut others out, and let your actions, not your slogans, do the talking.
